provenance: Frozen before weighted threshold selection. 13 real repository intelligence notes, one saved standing preference, three synthetic situational records. Agent-authored relevance labels require human judgement; no production accuracy claim. One separately frozen large-pool held-out scenario adds 30 explicitly irrelevant weather distractors to force lexical-only discovery for a current exact-symbol instruction after long background; all base scenarios retain the original corpus.
rubric: Relevant means direct useful implementation guidance for the concrete task. Adjacent subsystem knowledge is not automatically relevant. Recall standing preferences are unconditional and assessed separately. Recall filters labels to its ownership. BOTH reconciliation routes search both ownership partitions under existing service policy. Exact duplicates are a separate safety check and excluded from approximate scoring quality.
selectionRule: Calibration minimizes 2*falsePositive + falseNegative; ties prefer fewer false negatives then lower threshold. Experimental weights .25/.50/.25 fixed. Candidate limits S=20,L=20,C=4; floor disabled. TopN=3 recall,20 reconciliation. Promote only if every route heldout precision improves, recall decreases by no more than .05 and no-match FP does not increase; otherwise remain opt-in.

memories.text: For a durable model-managed workflow, extend the existing SessionApplication/tool pipeline and repository-bound Core/Persistence contracts rather than creating a separate model loop or store; inspect RepositoryIntelligenceOperations and the repository-intelligence path as the current example of provisional preparation, lifecycle rebinding, and atomic publication.

When a long-running feature must survive transient failure without exposing partial state, follow repository-intelligence onboarding: checkpoint provisional DTOs outside normal readers, revalidate current primary supports on resume, keep required coverage open, and publish through one atomic store commit only after completion gates pass.

When adding a built-in or imported model tool, register it in the shared ToolRegistry and route execution through ToolInvocationPipeline so repository trust, policy/approval, scheduling, hooks, activity, sanitization, budgets, cancellation, and provenance remain consistent; inspect MemoriesTool and MCP publication as representative consumers.

For model-facing prose, add or change a code-declared PromptAssetCatalog entry and deployed Markdown asset rather than embedding a new literal; keep the catalog, owning project deployment, token contract, docs/operations/prompts.md, docs/prompt-file-reference.md, and exact-bijection tests synchronized.

For user-visible application behavior, keep authority in host-owned commands/events and frontend-neutral coordination, then add an explicit consumer/output path in each intended frontend; semantic refresh demonstrates full TUI catalog/dispatch/projection and a shared HeadlessShell API, but not an executable headless refresh route.

Add lifecycle automation through HookCoordinator and its closed envelope/result contracts, not as an alternate policy or execution path: repository-hook handler outcomes stay advisory, only eligible external managed policy may block, and normalized invocations are durably audited; inspect persistence/subscriber failure handling separately because infrastructure failures are not normalized fail-open.

For MCP integrations, compose one McpManager/McpAdapter against the shared ToolRegistry and ToolInvocationPipeline; keep profiles, secrets/OAuth, transport bounds, generation-scoped publication, approval, draining, and cleanup host-owned rather than treating a server as a separate authority.

Implement model-requested file changes through SourceEditTool and SourceEditApplication: preserve workspace/path preconditions, stage and authorize the exact diff, commit transactionally with durable effects and events, then treat incremental semantic feedback as advisory; builds and tests remain explicit validation operations.

For an external extension, implement the small Threadsmith.Extensions.Abstractions contracts, exclude the abstractions DLL from the package, declare truthful capability resources/permissions, and let ExtensionHost/CapabilityProxy route tools through host policy while generation leases govern drain, deactivation, removal, and verified collectible-ALC unload.

When adding a model provider, register a provider-neutral compiled adapter through ModelProviderRegistry/ConfiguredModelProvider and keep SDK types, credentials, native replay, retry, streaming, and usage accounting inside the adapter; Anthropic is the example for user-owned secret discovery and retry only before visible output is delivered.

When making an operation observable, publish host-owned correlated domain events and extend the frontend-neutral projection/TUI presentation plus safe metadata-only telemetry; add command-specific headless result or transcript output explicitly because the TUI block formatter is not a general headless renderer.

For a compiler-aware capability, compose a bounded built-in tool over the shared semantic engines and ordinary registry/pipeline; preserve path filtering, provenance, immutable generations, confidence/omissions, and use SemanticEngine’s bounded abandon-and-discard path for non-cooperative compiler work instead of creating an independent workspace.

Add reusable workflows as bounded declarative skill packages only when their capabilities already exist as governed tools/actions; follow SkillCatalog discovery, SkillPackageVerifier trust/asset checks and exact-digest enablement, compatibility evaluation, SkillWorkflowOrchestrator checkpoints/resume, and ordinary tool policy instead of embedding scripts or private execution machinery.
Always address the user as "Your Grace".
